# Cases for the value of one query parameter. The Go decoder (internal/core) reads this file, and
# so does the codec of the browser (js/runtime/searchcodec.ts), run in Node and in beastjs. All must give
# the same answer for every line.
#
# Columns, separated by one tab:
#   type    string, bool, int, int8, int16, int32, int64, uint, uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64, uintptr or float
#           (the type of the field, float is a float64: a float32 field is a build error)
#   input   the value as a JSON string
#   result  ok when the value is a valid way to write one, x when it is not
#   bits    for ok: the 64 bits of the decoded number as 16 hex digits, 1 or 0 for a bool, - for a string
#
# A valid value is the only way to write it: decoding it and writing the result gives the text back.
# Every integer must also be at most 2^53-1 in size, the largest a browser holds exactly.
# What an empty value means (the field was not passed) is decided for the whole field, not here.
int	"0"	ok	0000000000000000
int	"-0"	x	-
int	"+0"	x	-
int	"00"	x	-
int	"01"	x	-
int	"-01"	x	-
int	"1"	ok	3ff0000000000000
int	"-1"	ok	bff0000000000000
int	"+1"	x	-
int	"007"	x	-
int	"12345"	ok	40c81c8000000000
int	"2"	ok	4000000000000000
int	"10"	ok	4024000000000000
